scenarios.prompt: Review this proposed implementation boundary without running commands. A PowerShell command is responsible for launching a child process, forwarding selected environment values, preserving stdout and stderr separately, and converting the child exit code into the command's public result. The repository needs regression coverage for success, nonzero exit, malformed output, environment restoration, and process cleanup. Decide the implementation owner, oracle, and test lane. Return exactly four labeled lines with no other prose: `Boundary: PowerShell`, `Owner: PowerShell-process-entry-point`, `Oracle: fresh-process-receipt`, and `Test: Pester-state-table`, one per line.

Review this proposed implementation boundary without running commands. A team wants a repository policy that understands YAML workflow mappings, sequences, booleans, nulls, comments, folded scalars, anchors, aliases, and duplicate keys. The proposal is a PowerShell regex and line parser because nearby validation scripts are PowerShell. Decide the implementation boundary, PowerShell's role, the oracle, and the first test. Return exactly four labeled lines with no other prose: `Boundary: maintained-YAML-parser`, `PowerShell-role: orchestration-only`, `Oracle: parser-DOM`, and `Test: mutation-before-fix`, one per line.

Measure and reduce runtime allocations in a PowerShell data-processing command under representative production inputs. Establish a baseline, isolate process state, validate outputs, and report uncertainty. This is application runtime performance, not PowerShell API or correctness design. Do not edit files or run commands. Return exactly these four labeled lines with no other prose: `Measurement: establish-baseline`, `Process-state: matched`, `Correctness: validate-output`, and `Uncertainty: report`, one per line.

Convert an existing Pester 5 test suite mechanically to Pester 6 syntax while preserving test intent. This is migration work, not a request to redesign production PowerShell, test ownership, or process semantics. Dedicated upstream pester-migration guidance owns it when available. Do not edit files or run commands. Return exactly these three labeled lines with no other prose: `Route: upstream-pester-migration`, `Scope: mechanical-v5-to-v6`, and `Redesign: not-requested`, one per line.

Review this PowerShell API refactor without running commands. An exported function already uses named-only binding. Its parameter names, types, parameter sets, mandatory status, validation, and defaults are documented. It emits one object with a documented property schema and uses a documented terminating error contract. The proposal changes only private implementation and preserves all of those behaviors. Decide the compatibility treatment and controls. Return exactly these four labeled lines with no other prose: `Compatibility: preserve`, `Parameters: snapshot-unchanged`, `Result: public-invocation-unchanged`, and `Migration: none`, one per line.

Review this proposed PowerShell API cleanup without running commands. An existing public script accepts a positional `-Configuration` parameter whose default is `Debug`, emits objects with `Path` and `Configuration`, and exits 2 for invalid input. The proposal disables positional binding, renames the parameter to `-Mode`, changes its default to `Release`, renames the output property to `Mode`, and changes that failure exit code to 1. Decide the compatibility treatment. Return exactly these four labeled lines with no other prose: `Compatibility: breaking-change`, `Parameters: binding-name-and-default-changed`, `Result: schema-and-exit-changed`, and `Action: name-break-and-migrate-callers`, one per line.

Review a PowerShell wrapper that reads JSON receipts without running commands. The required `passed` field must be a JSON Boolean: `false` is valid failure evidence, but missing, null, numeric `0`, empty text, and string `"false"` are invalid. A proposal uses `if ($receipt.passed)` and a regex over the JSON text. Decide the parser, validation, and negative controls. Return exactly these three labeled lines with no other prose: `Parser: structured-JSON`, `Validation: presence-and-Boolean-type`, and `Cases: false-distinct-from-missing-null-zero-empty-and-string`, one per line.

Review a PowerShell wrapper reading JSON objects with a required `items` array. It currently assigns `$items = if ($doc.Contains('items')) { $doc['items'] }` and observes that a parsed empty array appears as null and a one-item array as a scalar. Missing `items` must not be mistaken for a present empty array. Without running commands or editing files, decide how to retain presence and shape and what to test. Return exactly these four labeled lines with no other prose: `Presence: test-key-exists`, `Retrieval: direct-array-reference`, `Output: avoid-pipeline-enumeration`, and `Cases: missing-empty-single-multiple`, one per line.

Design tests without running commands for a PowerShell module function that processes pipeline items. The independent contract sends valid items to the success stream and rejects invalid items without putting them on that stream. Existing Pester tests only assert that some output is nonempty, so letting an invalid item through would still pass. Choose the owning harness, oracle, cases, and a reversible negative control. Return exactly four labeled lines with no other prose: `Harness: Pester-6`, `Oracle: independent-input-output-table`, `Cases: valid-and-invalid-pipeline-items`, and `Negative-control: invalid-item-on-success-must-fail`, one per line.

Review a PowerShell component's Pester 6 validation without running commands. A test filter selects no cases, the test process exits 0, and a summary treats zero failures as a passing check. It also counts skipped tests as passed and ignores inconclusive tests, failed blocks or containers, and infrastructure failures. A result marked Failed, an incomplete worker, or a nonzero exit code must not count as a pass even when the counts appear valid. Decide the execution lane, status and process gates, discovery gate, count accounting, failure checks, and negative control needed before reporting validation. Return exactly seven labeled lines with no other prose: `Run: isolated-Pester-6`, `Result: require-Passed`, `Worker: complete-with-exit-zero`, `Discovery: require-positive-count`, `Counts: reconcile-passed-failed-skipped-not-run-inconclusive`, `Failures: reject-failed-blocks-containers-and-infrastructure`, and `Negative-control: empty-selection-must-fail`, one per line.
